mainTopic: Whether שביעית holiness transfers by חילול or only by מקח (רב אשי's two versions), then רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות of זכר למקדש: לולב for seven days and the whole of יום הנף.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the debate between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. The question is whether the קדושה of שביעית moves to a new item only by מקח (purchase), or also by חילול (redemption). רב אשי first says they argue only about פרי ראשון, the original fruit. רבינא disproves this from a ברייתא about a סלע of שביעית, where only a purchase works. So רב אשי flips his view: they argue only about פרי שני, and for the original fruit everyone requires מקח. A ברייתא that says 'שביעית' can be redeemed onto animals is read as דמי שביעית, the money of שביעית, just as 'מעשר' in the same ברייתא must mean מעשר money. Then a new משנה teaches two תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי after the חורבן: taking the לולב for seven days everywhere, and forbidding חדש for all of יום הנף. The גמרא learns the idea of זכר למקדש from the פסוק 'ציון היא דורש אין לה'. It then explains the יום הנף rule as a safeguard for when the מקדש is rebuilt. Finally, רב נחמן בר יצחק says the rule follows רבי יהודה, who holds that the prohibition is from the Torah; his proof verse continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The animal dispute is only about males; with females everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies the ברייתא about redeeming שביעית and מעשר שני onto animals. The argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is only about male animals. With female animals, everyone agrees: redemption onto slaughtered animals works, onto live ones it does not, because of a גזירה that he might raise flocks from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument is about male animals. But with female animals, everyone agrees: produce can be redeemed onto slaughtered animals, but not onto live animals. This is a rabbinic decree, out of concern that he might raise whole flocks from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of a ברייתא (quoted on the previous amud) that limits the argument about live animals to males only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live female animal will give birth, so the holy value would get stuck in a growing herd that cannot easily be eaten in קדושה. That is why everyone forbids live females, and the חכמים extended the גזירה to males too. The key point for the bigger sugya is the ברייתא's language. It says 'מתחללין' (redeemed) and not 'purchased', which suggests שביעית can transfer by חילול. That supports רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Are redeemed; the holiness transfers onto them

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The word 'בזכרים' finishes a statement from the previous page: 'The argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is only about males.'
steps.whyThisMatters: The word 'מתחללין' in this ברייתא is what later forces רב אשי to explain how it fits his final position (Step 6).

phrases.english: [The dispute is] with males, but with females —
phrases.notes: Continues from the previous daf: the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is limited to male animals.

phrases.english: everyone agrees:
onto slaughtered ones — they are redeemed,
onto live ones — they are not redeemed,
a decree, lest he raise flocks from them.
phrases.notes: Females give birth, so the holy value would become a growing herd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the ברייתא from the end of the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With female animals, all agree: redemption onto slaughtered animals works, onto live animals it does not, because of the herd-raising גזירה.

steps.title: רב אשי's first proposal: the dispute is only about the original fruit
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proposes that the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר is only about פרי ראשון. For פרי שני, everyone agrees the קדושה transfers by both מקח and חילול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The argument is about the first (original) fruit. But with the second fruit, everyone agrees: it works both by purchase and by redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tries to narrow the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. He says they argue only about the original שביעית fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרי ראשון is the actual שביעית produce. פרי שני is whatever was gotten in exchange for it, such as money. רב אשי's idea: רבי אלעזר requires מקח only for the original fruit. Once you reach the exchanged item, even רבי אלעזר agrees that חילול works too.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא, major editor of the בבלי
The item received in exchange for שביעית produce
By way of a purchase or trade
By way of redemption, transferring the holiness

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists of terms. 'פרי ראשון / פרי שני' is about which item you are dealing with. 'מקח / חילול' is about how the holiness moves.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
the dispute is about the first fruit,
but about the second fruit — everyone agrees:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ חִילּוּל.
phrases.english: both by way of purchase and by way of redemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בִּפְרִי רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the animal ברייתא to defining exactly where רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute concerns פרי ראשון; for פרי שני, both מקח and חילול work according to everyone.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא kept saying 'purchased'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי handles a ברייתא that says 'לקח' even for פרי שני, which seems to mean only מקח works. He answers that the ברייתא used 'לקח' in the second clause only to match the first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the fact that the ברייתא says 'he bought', 'he bought': since it taught 'he bought' in the first part, it also taught 'he bought' in the last part.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי blocks a possible challenge. The ברייתא that supports רבי אלעזר uses the word 'bought' even for the second fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא says 'bought' about פרי שני, it could imply that only מקח works there. רב אשי answers that the word is just matching style. The first clause needed 'לקח' (for פרי ראשון), so the תנא repeated it in the second clause. That repetition does not exclude חילול.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause / the last clause of a text

phrases.english: And that which it teaches 'he bought', 'he bought' —
since it taught 'he bought' in the first clause,
it also taught 'he bought' in the last clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends Step 2 against a wording-based objection from רבי אלעזר's ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'לקח' in the second clause shows that only מקח works for פרי שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word is repeated only to match the first clause, so it does not rule out חילול.

steps.title: רבינא objects from the case of the סלע of שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבינא cites a ברייתא about someone with a סלע of שביעית who wants to buy a garment. He must use a purchase-and-gift trick with a storekeeper. The סלע is פרי שני, yet the ברייתא allows only מקח, not חילול. That contradicts רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged רב אשי: Someone has a סלע of שביעית and wants to buy a shirt with it. What should he do? He goes to his regular storekeeper and says, 'Give me fruit for this סלע.' The storekeeper gives it to him. Then he says, 'These fruits are yours as a gift.' The storekeeper says, 'Here is this סלע for you as a gift.' Now he can buy whatever he wants with it. But here the סלע is the second fruit, and the ברייתא teaches that purchase works, but redemption does not!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a ברייתא to attack רב אשי's claim that everyone allows חילול for פרי שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סלע got its קדושה by being exchanged for שביעית produce, so it is פרי שני. If חילול worked for פרי שני, the owner could just redeem the coin onto fruit. Instead, the ברייתא requires a real purchase, then gifts back and forth to recover a non-holy coin. So for פרי שני only מקח works, against רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source)
A coin that carries שביעית holiness

steps.confusionAlert: The gifts are not the transfer itself. The holiness moves from the coin to the fruit through the purchase. The gifts are only a friendly way for the owner to get his now non-holy coin back.

phrases.english: Ravina challenged Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סֶלַע שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית
phrases.english: one who has a sela of the Sabbatical Year
and wishes to buy a garment with it,
what should he do?
He should go to the storekeeper he regularly uses,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי בְּסֶלַע פֵּירוֹת,
phrases.english: and say to him: Give me fruit for a sela,
and he gives him,
and he then says to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי פֵּירוֹת הַלָּלוּ נְתוּנִים לְךָ בְּמַתָּנָה.
phrases.english: These fruits are given to you as a gift.
phrases.notes: The fruits now carry שביעית holiness, and the storekeeper eats them accordingly.

phrases.english: And he [the storekeeper] says to him:
Here is this sela for you as a gift,
and that one buys with it whatever he wants.
But here, it is second fruit,
and it teaches: by way of purchase — yes,
by way of redemption — no!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that for פרי שני everyone allows חילול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סלע is פרי שני, yet the ברייתא requires a real purchase and does not allow חילול.

steps.title: רב אשי reverses: the dispute is about the second fruit
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי flips his position. The מחלוקת is about פרי שני. For פרי ראשון, everyone agrees that only מקח works, not חילול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: The argument is about the second fruit. But with the first fruit, everyone agrees: by purchase, yes; by redemption, no.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of רבינא's challenge, רב אשי gives the opposite version of his idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the original שביעית fruit can transfer its קדושה only through a sale, according to everyone. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue only about the exchanged item. The סלע ברייתא (only מקח for פרי שני) can now follow רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals a retraction and a new version)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch. In Step 2, the dispute was about the first fruit. Now it is about the second fruit, and the 'everyone agrees' part now says the opposite (only מקח).

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
the dispute is about the second fruit,
but about the first fruit, everyone agrees:
by way of purchase — yes,
by way of redemption — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בִּפְרִי שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's קשיא by reversing רב אשי's original proposal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute is about פרי ראשון, and for פרי שני everyone allows חילול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about פרי שני; for פרי ראשון, everyone requires מקח.

steps.title: 'שביעית' in the ברייתא means דמי שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's new position seems to clash with the ברייתא from Step 1, which says שביעית is redeemed (מתחלל) onto animals. רב אשי explains that 'שביעית' there means דמי שביעית, which is פרי שני. That is where רבי יוחנן allows חילול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא that teaches 'both שביעית and מעשר שני [are redeemed]': what does 'שביעית' mean? The money of שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains away a ברייתא that seemed to allow חילול for the original שביעית fruit, which would contradict his new position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new version, nobody allows חילול for פרי ראשון. Yet the animal ברייתא says 'שביעית' can be מתחלל. רב אשי reads 'שביעית' as money that came from שביעית fruit, which is פרי שני. So the ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute about פרי שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Money received in exchange for שביעית produce
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's final position: For the original שביעית fruit, everyone agrees only a purchase (מקח) transfers the קדושה. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue only about the exchanged item (פרי שני). The ברייתא saying 'שביעית is redeemed' refers to דמי שביעית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic map: חילול of שביעית is debated only for the exchanged value, never for the original produce.

phrases.english: And that which it teaches:
both Sabbatical-Year and second tithe [are redeemed] —
phrases.notes: Refers to the animal ברייתא explained in Step 1.

phrases.english: what is 'Sabbatical-Year'? Money of the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי: אֶחָד שְׁבִיעִית וְאֶחָד מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב אשי's revised position (Step 5) against the ברייתא from Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a term in the source (אוקימתא of wording)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שביעית' in the ברייתא means the original produce, so חילול would work for פרי ראשון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שביעית' means דמי שביעית (פרי שני), where רבי יוחנן allows חילול.

steps.title: Proof that 'Tithe' in the ברייתא Means Tithe Money
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא mentions מעשר, and that word cannot mean actual מעשר שני produce. The Torah requires מעשר שני produce to be redeemed only onto silver coins. So 'מעשר' must mean דמי מעשר, and likewise 'שביעית' must mean דמי שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, would 'tithe' mean actual tithe produce? But it is written: 'And you shall bind up the money in your hand.' Rather, it must mean tithe money. Here too, it means שביעית money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב אשי's answer from Step 6. It points to the word 'מעשר' in the same ברייתא, which clearly has to mean money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that both items can be redeemed onto an animal. Actual מעשר שני produce can only be redeemed onto coins ('וצרת הכסף'), so the ברייתא must be speaking about the money. Since 'מעשר' in that ברייתא means דמי מעשר, it is reasonable to read 'שביעית' in the same ברייתא as דמי שביעית too.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so: introduces a proof by showing the alternative cannot work
'Bind up the money in your hand': the פסוק showing מעשר שני produce is redeemed onto coins
Money that has taken on the status of מעשר שני
Here too: applies the same reasoning to a parallel case

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רב אשי holds that the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר is about פרי שני (money). The ברייתא that allows חילול onto animals is speaking about דמי שביעית, just as it speaks about דמי מעשר.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
would 'tithe' mean actual tithe produce?
phrases.notes: This refers to מעשר שני mentioned in the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: But it is written: 'And you shall bind up the money in your hand.'
phrases.notes: Produce of מעשר שני is redeemed onto coins, not onto animals.

phrases.english: Rather, it must mean tithe money.
Here too, it means Sabbatical-Year money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reinterpretation in Step 6 by drawing a parallel from the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Reading 'שביעית' in the ברייתא as דמי שביעית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'מעשר' in the same ברייתא, together with the פסוק 'וצרת הכסף בידך'

steps.title: משנה: Taking the לולב Seven Days After the Destruction
steps.stepSummary: Before the חורבן, the לולב was taken seven days in the מקדש and only one day elsewhere. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled that it should be taken seven days everywhere, as a זכר למקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Originally, the לולב was taken in the מקדש for seven days and in the outlying areas for one day. Once the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted that the לולב be taken in the outlying areas for seven days, in memory of the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It describes how the מצוה of לולב changed after the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the לולב is taken seven days only in the מקדש, and only the first day elsewhere. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי extended the seven days to everywhere so that people would keep remembering the מקדש. The Torah obligation itself did not change; this is a rabbinic תקנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The area outside the מקדש (not 'country' in the modern sense)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מדינה' does not mean a state or province. It means anywhere outside the מקדש. The days after the first day of לולב outside the מקדש are only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Originally the lulav was taken
in the Temple for seven days,
and in the outlying areas for one day.
Once the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted
that the lulav be taken in the outlying areas for seven days,
in remembrance of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; unrelated to the preceding שביעית discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, the לולב is taken seven days everywhere as a זכר למקדש.

steps.title: משנה: The Whole Day of Waving Stays Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי also ruled that new grain (חדש) stays forbidden for the entire יום הנף (16 ניסן), even though there is no longer an עומר offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he instituted that the entire day of waving should be forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. This one is about when new grain may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New grain becomes permitted once the עומר is waved on 16 ניסן. Without a מקדש, it would be permitted from dawn (האיר מזרח) of that day. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade it for that entire day, so it is only permitted from 17 ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of waving the עומר: 16 ניסן
The barley offering whose waving permits new grain
New-crop grain, forbidden until the עומר

steps.confusionAlert: 'אסור' here does not mean the day itself is forbidden in some general way. It means eating חדש is forbidden for that whole day.

phrases.english: And that the day of waving
should be entirely forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second תקנה of the same רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חדש remains forbidden for the entire 16 ניסן even after the חורבן.

steps.title: Source for Making a Remembrance of the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that it is proper to make practices as a זכר למקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that we make practices in remembrance of the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for a source. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes that a זכר למקדש is a valid reason for a תקנה. The גמרא wants a basis in a פסוק for this idea.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know
that we act in remembrance of the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the משנה's reason 'זכר למקדש'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source for making practices as a זכר למקדש.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'No One Seeks Her' Means She Needs Seeking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן cites ירמיהו's complaint that 'ציון has no one who seeks her.' This implies that ציון should be sought and remembered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: As the פסוק says: 'For I will bring healing to you and heal you of your wounds, says ה׳, because they called you an outcast: it is ציון, no one seeks her.' 'No one seeks her' implies that she needs seeking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question from Step 10 with a פסוק. He learns from its criticism what we are supposed to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא criticizes the people because 'no one seeks' ציון. From this criticism (מכלל), we learn that ציון should be sought, meaning remembered and cared about. This is the basis for רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות as a זכר למקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: inferring a positive rule from a negative statement

steps.whatToRemember: A זכר למקדש is rooted in the פסוק 'ציון היא דורש אין לה'. We are obligated to 'seek' ציון, so חז״ל made תקנות such as seven days of לולב everywhere and the whole יום הנף being forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is the general basis for many practices done as a זכר למקדש or זכר לחורבן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: As the verse states:
'For I will bring healing to you
and heal you of your wounds, says the Lord,
because they called you an outcast:
it is Zion, no one seeks her.'
'No one seeks her'
implies that she requires seeking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's complaint 'דורש אין לה' implies a duty to seek and remember ציון, which supports making a זכר למקדש.

steps.title: Why forbid new grain the whole day of waving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that חדש is forbidden for all of יום הנף and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that the entire day of waving should be forbidden. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule about יום הנף and asks why he made it. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no עומר being brought, you might expect חדש to become permitted at dawn on 16 ניסן. Yet רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the entire day. The גמרא wants to know what this stricter rule is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of waving the עומר, which is 16 ניסן
New-crop grain, which is forbidden until the עומר permits it

phrases.english: And that the day of waving should be [entirely forbidden].
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling about יום הנף from step 9 and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind forbidding חדש for all of 16 ניסן

steps.title: People may get confused once the בית המקדש is rebuilt
steps.stepSummary: The rule exists so that, once the בית המקדש is rebuilt, people will not eat חדש at dawn out of habit from the year before.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בית המקדש will soon be rebuilt. People will say: 'Last year, didn't we eat as soon as the eastern sky lit up? Let us eat now too.' They do not realize the difference. Last year there was no בית המקדש, so dawn made the grain permitted. Now that there is a בית המקדש, only the עומר makes it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that this is a protective rule. It keeps people from building a habit that would mislead them once the בית המקדש returns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a מקדש, חדש really is permitted from dawn on the 16th. With a מקדש, it is permitted only after the עומר is brought. If people got used to eating at dawn, they would keep doing so after the rebuilding, which would be forbidden. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the whole day ahead of time.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern sky lit up, meaning dawn
The עומר offering makes the new grain permitted

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'permitters.' Dawn permits חדש only when there is no מקדש. When there is a מקדש, only the actual עומר offering permits it.

phrases.english: Soon the Temple will be rebuilt,
and they will say: Last year,
didn't we eat as soon as the east lit up?
Now too, let us eat.
But they do not know
that last year, when there was no Temple,
the lighting of the east permitted it.
Now that there is a Temple,
the עומר permits it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a protective rule (גזירה) against eating at dawn by habit after the בית המקדש is rebuilt.

steps.title: When would the rebuilding have to happen for this mistake to occur?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that no timing of the rebuilding seems to justify forbidding the entire day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When would the בית המקדש be rebuilt? If you say it is rebuilt on the 16th, then dawn already permitted the grain, since there was no מקדש at dawn. But if it is rebuilt on the 15th, the grain should be permitted from midday onward. We learned in a משנה: those who live far away may eat from midday onward, because the בית דין is not lazy about bringing the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason just given. It checks every possible day of rebuilding and finds that forbidding the whole day does not seem necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rebuilding is on the 16th, dawn came before any מקדש existed, so the grain was already permitted. If it is on the 15th or earlier, the עומר will surely be brought by midday. That would make the afternoon permitted, so at most the morning should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who live far from ירושלים
Being lazy or putting things off

phrases.english: It is rebuilt when?
If you say that it is rebuilt on the sixteenth,
the lighting of the east already permitted it!
Rather, say that it is rebuilt on the fifteenth;
then from midday onward it should be permitted,
for we learned: Those who are far away
are permitted from midday onward,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מִתְעַצְּלִים בּוֹ!
phrases.english: because the court is not lazy about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the confusion after rebuilding justifies forbidding the entire day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rebuilt on the 16th: dawn already permitted. Rebuilt on the 15th: the עומר is brought by midday, so the afternoon should be permitted.

steps.title: The case is a rebuilding at night or near sunset
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a rebuilding on the night of the 16th, or just before sunset on the 15th, when the עומר cannot be prepared in time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for a case where the בית המקדש is rebuilt at night. Or, alternatively, where it is rebuilt close to sunset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It identifies a specific timing where the mistake really could happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rebuilding happens at night or right before sunset, there is not enough time to get the עומר ready by midday. People would see midday arrive and eat, even though the עומר had not been brought. So the whole day had to be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

phrases.english: It is needed only where it is rebuilt at night,
or alternatively, close to sunset.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing to a specific case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any timing of the rebuilding would make forbidding the whole day unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rebuilding at night or near sunset leaves no time to bring the עומר by midday, so the whole day must be forbidden.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the prohibition is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the rule is not a protective rule at all. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was following רבי יהודה, who holds that חדש is forbidden all of the 16th by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said this following the view of רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה says it is forbidden by Torah law, as it is written...
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives a completely new reason for the rule. The verse that proves it begins on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer treated the rule as a rabbinic safeguard for the future. רב נחמן בר יצחק says that without a עומר, the Torah itself forbids חדש for the whole day of the 16th, according to רבי יהודה. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was not adding anything; he was simply stating the Torah's law.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view is followed here

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the category of the rule. It is no longer a rabbinic safeguard (גזירה) but a Torah-level prohibition, which affects how strictly it applies.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
said it following the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: It is forbidden by Torah law,
as it is written:
phrases.notes: The verse continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 12, replacing the protective-rule explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule follows רבי יהודה, who holds that חדש is forbidden all of the 16th by Torah law.
